clips.send: Someone trying intermittent fasting sends this to their gym-buddy group chat: the protein number nobody mentioned, before they waste another fast - the anxiety of doing it wrong.
clips.caption:
Dr. Daniel Pompa told Kevin Trudeau where 'partial fasting' actually came from: a Frenchman named Albert Mazer, who used it to slowly refeed people who had been very sick, and found they kept improving the longer he went.

Pompa's own rule for it: 500 to 1,200 calories a day depending on body size, and under 20 grams of protein. Stay under that line and your body still gets autophagy - clearing out old, damaged cells for energy while you fast.

Go over on protein, he says, and that switch never flips.

Ever tried fasting and wondered if you were doing it right?
